name: Aatrox
notes: Casts go one at a time: one busy_until timer tracks the champion's current cast, and no other cast or attack starts inside it. World Ender is cast first at t=0 (its 0.25 s cast time, during which nothing else starts) to secure its bonus AD for as much of the fight as possible; Q and W read their AD-scaling damage from Aatrox's current total AD at the moment they land, so the R buff amplifies them too, per the mechanic that Q/W damage is calculated from current stats.

Deathbringer Stance (P) is assumed pre-charged and ready at t=0 (the more common reading for a level-16 fight); each landed basic attack that does not consume it reduces its remaining cooldown by 2s, and a landed Q cast (assumed sweetspot, see below) or W hit reduces it by 2s/4s respectively; consuming it resets the cooldown to the full level-based value.

Every Darkin Blade (Q) cast is assumed to land its Sweetspot against the stationary dummy (maximum damage reading, doubling the Deathbringer Stance cooldown refund on each cast); each cast has a 0.6s cast time (no other cast or attack starts inside it), and the three casts are chained back-to-back at the 1-second static gap between casts (unaffected by ability haste), which is longer than the cast time so the gap alone paces them.

Infernal Chains (W) is cast on cooldown, with a 0.25s cast time (busy until it ends); since the dummy never moves the 1.5s tether always survives, so both the initial hit and the delayed pull hit land, each dealing the base+40% AD physical damage (the wiki's literal 'the same damage again' reading) and each independently refunding 2s of Deathbringer Stance cooldown; the delayed pull is a scheduled effect, not a new cast, so it does not itself hold up other casts.

Umbral Dash (E) deals no damage and is used purely as an attack-timer reset, cast the instant it is off cooldown (and not inside another cast) to squeeze in an extra basic attack; it has no cast time and costs nothing. Its passive lifesteal-style heal never changes damage dealt so it is ignored.
Mana is not modeled: none of Aatrox's abilities cost mana in this data set.
